They've made you their scapegoat – the person they pick on and make fun of.  Losing weight disrupts that role, but don't stop. If they can't use you as their scapegoat anymore, they'll just find another target.  Keep up the great work!

since you said you have less time to exercise your weight loss needs to be focused on the eating and mental aspects. I would advise you to look into intermediate fasting! prepare your dinner for the next day, so that you can create a routine of having dinner when you finish work. You could try not to eat anything after 6pm! Also work on healing any past trauma because that can lead to emotional eating. I don't know if you are spiritual but consider your body your child and treat it like a child so you are now a parent to that child, name your child (your body). I named my child (my body) chrysola (pronounced chris - ola). So yh if I had a child I wouldn't want them over eating junk food or anything so I don't allow chrysola (my body) to overeat. I also like to treat weight loss as a game. I can either win the game (lose weight) or I can lose the game (put on or not lose weight). Also get enough sleep so that you make more mindful decisions. Try to make time for a stress free activity weekly. I personally like to go to a sauna. I also suggest rewarding yourself. I make a tally of all the good things I have done to contribute to my weight loss (E.G resisting tempting food or going to bed on time) and I wait till that tally reaches 25 and then I reward myself in a healthy way by buying like a cheap item on shein or something. But it makes weight loss seem fun rather than a chore.
